title: Supernova Neutrinos and the Origin of Biomolecular Homochirality
authors: Amirmasoud Jannat, Soroush Shakeri, Farhad Shahbazi
abstract: We investigate the role of parity-violating interactions between supernova neutrinos and chiral molecules in nearby interstellar molecular clouds as a potential source of biomolecular homochirality. We introduce neutrino interactions into the autocatalytic chemical reactions in a far-from-equilibrium noise-induced system. These interactions create a directional bias between L and D enantiomers in the racemization reactions, which is amplified by autocatalysis and stochastic fluctuations. We solve the stochastic equations within the Ito sense to obtain the dynamics of the probability distribution of the enantiomeric excesses, offering an astrophysical scenario for the delivery of homochirality seeds to Earth by meteorites. In spite of the weak interactions of supernova neutrinos, our framework introduces an amplification mechanism to yield a considerable enantiomeric excess of more than $10\%$, in agreement with the latest chemical analysis of the meteorites. Moreover, we scan over the parameter space of the model, inferring from the observational values in order to explore the window of opportunity to generate the initial seeds of homochiral states in interstellar molecular clouds.
summary: This paper proposes that supernova neutrinos can act as a source for the initial seeds of life's chirality. By coupling parity-violating neutrino interactions into autocatalytic chemical reactions within interstellar clouds, the authors show that tiny directional biases are amplified by non-equilibrium dynamics to produce significant homochirality.
main_problem: The study investigates whether parity-violating interactions from supernova neutrinos can provide an astrophysical mechanism to generate the necessary homochirality in interstellar molecular clouds.
main_result: The combination of neutrino-induced directional bias, autocatalysis, and stochastic fluctuations allows for an amplification mechanism that predicts an enantiomeric excess greater than 10%, consistent with meteorite analyses.
method: The authors solve stochastic differential equations (in the Itô sense) derived from a chemical reaction scheme incorporating parity-violating energy differences ($\Delta E_{PV}$).
model_or_system: The model describes autocatalytic chemical reactions in an Interstellar Molecular Cloud near a supernova, where neutrino interactions introduce a directional bias term into the system dynamics.
key_observables: Enantiomeric excess (ee) of chiral molecules ($\omega$), and the probability distribution of this excess over time.
important_parameters: Neutrino flux ($10^{33}-10^{35} 	ext{ cm}^{-2}	ext{s}^{-1}$), Supernova Luminosity ($\sim 10^{51} - 10^{53} 	ext{ erg/s}$), and the Parity Violation Energy Difference ($\Delta E_{PV}$).
main_assumptions: The neutrino interaction term is treated as a deterministic component of the chemical scheme, and approximations are made for calculating $\Delta E_{PV}$ using DFT methods.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the chemical reaction schemes (including autocatalytic, decay, and neutrino-induced steps) and show time evolution plots detailing how the mean enantiomeric excess ($\langle \omega angle$) changes with temperature or time.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the physical context (neutrino interaction Hamiltonian), developing the stochastic chemical model using Master/Fokker-Planck equations, and finally simulating the thermal evolution to demonstrate how symmetry breaking leads to high enantiomeric excess.
why_interesting: This work models non-equilibrium chemical dynamics driven by an external, weak quantum field effect (neutrinos) acting on chiral systems, which is a prime example of open quantum system dynamics in a far-from-equilibrium setting.
